grammarFocus: 转述动词；引述与改写；限定词 some / most / all 的范围。
title: The Community Archive Project: Evidence and Memory
instructions: 阅读以下关于社区档案项目的文章，回答10个问题。文章为模拟教育材料，非真实事件。注意转述动词和限定词（some/most/all）的用法。
passage:
In the small town of Millbrook, a group of residents decided to create a community archive. The project aimed to collect stories, photographs, and documents from local families. The coordinator, Emma, explained that the archive would help future generations understand the town's history. She said, "We want to preserve the everyday experiences of ordinary people."

Some volunteers were skeptical at first. They argued that the project would take too much time and that few people would contribute. However, most residents supported the idea. They believed that the archive could strengthen community bonds. One volunteer, Tom, admitted, "I wasn't sure at first, but now I think it's a great way to connect with neighbors."

All the materials were stored in the old library building. The team digitized most of the photographs and documents. They claimed that digitization would make the collection accessible to everyone. However, some elderly residents insisted that physical copies were still important. They pointed out that not everyone had internet access.

The project faced a challenge when a local historian questioned the accuracy of some stories. She warned that memories could be unreliable. In response, the team introduced a verification process. They asked contributors to provide additional evidence, such as letters or official records. Emma stated, "We don't want to present fiction as fact. Accuracy is crucial."

Most contributors welcomed the verification step. They felt it added credibility to the archive. A few, however, found it cumbersome. One contributor complained, "It's too much paperwork. I just wanted to share my grandmother's story." The team acknowledged this concern but maintained that evidence was necessary.

After six months, the archive had collected over 200 items. The team reported that all items had been cataloged and most had been digitized. They announced that the archive would open to the public in the spring. Some residents planned to visit regularly, while others remained indifferent. Overall, the project was considered a success. Emma concluded, "We've learned that listening to different voices is essential. Some stories may be challenged, but that's part of the process."

The archive now serves as a resource for local schools. Teachers mention that students enjoy exploring the primary sources. The team hopes to expand the project to neighboring towns. They emphasize that community involvement is key. As Emma put it, "It's not just about the past; it's about building a shared future."

Looking back, the team reflected on the lessons learned. They noted that some initial fears about low participation had been unfounded; in fact, many residents contributed multiple items. The verification process, while time-consuming, had improved the quality of the collection. Most importantly, the project had fostered a sense of shared ownership. As one volunteer remarked, "We all learned that history is not just about dates and names; it's about people's lives." The archive continues to grow, with new contributions arriving each month. The team also plans to hold workshops to train volunteers in interviewing techniques and to ensure that all future contributions meet the same standards of evidence. They believe that by involving more residents, the archive will become an even richer resource for the community. In addition, the team is considering creating a digital map that shows where each item came from, so that users can explore the town's history geographically. This idea has generated excitement among local teachers, who see it as a valuable tool for classroom projects. The archive's success has also inspired other nearby towns to start similar initiatives, and Emma has been invited to share her experience at a regional meeting. She emphasizes that the key to success is listening to the community and being transparent about the verification process. As the project moves forward, the team remains committed to balancing enthusiasm with accuracy, ensuring that the archive remains a trusted source of local history for generations to come.

questions.prompt: What did Emma say about the purpose of the archive?
options: To preserve the everyday experiences of ordinary people
To make money from historical documents
To compete with other towns' archives
answers: To preserve the everyday experiences of ordinary people
questions.explanation: 文章第一段中Emma说："We want to preserve the everyday experiences of ordinary people." 因此选A。
questions.evidence: We want to preserve the everyday experiences of ordinary people.

questions.prompt: How did most residents react to the project initially?
questions.explanation: 第二段提到："most residents supported the idea." 因此选B。

questions.prompt: What did the team digitize? (Answer with one word from the text)
questions.explanation: 第三段说："The team digitized most of the photographs and documents." 因此填photographs。
questions.evidence: The team digitized most of the photographs and documents.

questions.prompt: Why did some elderly residents insist on physical copies?
options: They did not trust digital files.
They did not have internet access.
answers: They did not have internet access.
questions.explanation: 第三段提到："They pointed out that not everyone had internet access." 因此选B。
questions.evidence: They pointed out that not everyone had internet access.

questions.prompt: What did the local historian warn about?
questions.explanation: 第四段中历史学家警告："She warned that memories could be unreliable." 因此选B。
questions.evidence: She warned that memories could be unreliable.

questions.prompt: What did the team introduce in response to the historian's concern?
questions.explanation: 第四段说："the team introduced a verification process." 因此选B。
questions.evidence: the team introduced a verification process.

questions.prompt: How did most contributors feel about the verification step?
questions.explanation: 第五段提到："Most contributors welcomed the verification step." 因此选A。
questions.evidence: Most contributors welcomed the verification step.

questions.prompt: How many items had the archive collected after six months? (Answer with a number)
questions.explanation: 第六段说："the archive had collected over 200 items." 因此填200。
questions.evidence: the archive had collected over 200 items.

questions.prompt: According to the text, all items had been cataloged.
questions.explanation: 第六段明确说："all items had been cataloged"，因此该陈述为真。

questions.prompt: The project will expand to neighboring towns next year.
questions.explanation: 文章最后一段提到"The team hopes to expand the project to neighboring towns." 但并未提及具体时间"next year"，因此该信息未给出。
questions.evidence: The team hopes to expand the project to neighboring towns.

grammar.title: 转述动词与限定词的范围
grammar.explanation: 转述动词如say, explain, argue, claim等用于引述他人的话。限定词some, most, all表示范围：some表示“一些”，most表示“大多数”，all表示“全部”。注意它们在句中的位置和含义。
grammar.example: She said, "We want to preserve the everyday experiences of ordinary people."

options: She said that she wanted to help.
She said that she wants to help.
She said that she want to help.
She said that she is wanting to help.
answers: She said that she wanted to help.
questions.explanation: 转述过去的话时，时态通常要后退一步，said后接that从句，动词用过去式。

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence? '_____ of the students passed the exam.' (meaning: all)
questions.explanation: 根据括号提示“all”，应选All表示全部。

questions.prompt: Choose the correct reported speech: 'I am tired,' she said.
questions.explanation: 直接引语中的am在转述时变为was，保持时态一致。
Most直接修饰复数名词时不用of，如most people；若用of则需加the，如most of the people。但本题要求选择正确用法，只有'Most people agreed.'是标准表达。
